top_choice_rationale: The optical lattice clock rests on a distinct physical idea, magic-wavelength trapping of many neutral atoms, that goes beyond the earlier comb and ion-control prizes. It has been verified across independent laboratories at the 10^-18 level and now yields clues from nature: gravitational redshift at millimetre scales, many-body effects and constraints on fundamental constants. The Katori and Ye allocation and the citation scope are well matched to the invention and its realisation.
